RagShortTexts: In 1268 at Tagliacozzo, Charles of Anjou ambushed young Conradin, executing the last.

Variants.Content: Fought on August 23, 1268, Tagliacozzo extinguished the imperial line of Frederick II. Sixteen-year-old Conradin swept away the Angevin frontline, only to be crushed by veteran crusader Érard de Valéry's concealed knightly reserve. Captured fleeing north, Conradin was publicly beheaded in Naples.
Conradin's thrown glove sparked the Sicilian Vespers decades later, transferring Staufen claims to Aragon.
